name: Washington
standard: WCAG 2.2 AA from 2026-07-01 (was WCAG 2.1 AA): WaTech policy USER-01 and standard USER-01-01-S, replacing OCIO Policy 188

laws.summary: Gives WaTech governance authority to set statewide IT policies and standards, including USER-01.

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web/mobile rule, 2024; compliance dates extended by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
laws.summary: Requires state and local government web content and mobile apps to conform to WCAG 2.1 AA, with compliance dates now 2027-04-26 (population 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

policy_docs.title: USER-01 Digital Accessibility Policy (adopted 2024-12-10; replaces Policy 188)

applies_to: State agencies as defined in RCW 43.105.020(22), with application to higher education, the legislature and the judiciary per RCW 43.105.052. Covers public-facing sites, apps, documents, media, blogs and social media, plus listed internal content. Local governments via the ADA Title II floor.

deadlines.what: Minimum standard rises to WCAG 2.2 AA (USER-01-01-S §3).
ADA Title II floor: state government and local entities with population 50,000+ must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24 by the 2026 DOJ IFR).
ADA Title II floor: local entities under 50,000 population and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26).
All content and tools employees or users need for essential duties or program participation must be accessible or have equivalent access (USER-01 §5).

requires: Agency digital accessibility policy defining roles, including the coordinator
IT accessibility coordinator as key contact and for complaint resolution; publish contact info
IT Accessibility Plan updated at least annually, prioritized with input from people with lived experience; public version posted
Documented annual accessibility awareness training for all employees, plus role-based training
Equivalent access where technology cannot be made compliant
Processes to ensure new covered technology is accessible
mobile: explicit — covered technology includes 'applications', and exceptions track the DOJ web/mobile rule.
procurement: Accessibility requirements in procurement, scope and budget; validation by human user testing plus a third-party report, VPAT or compliance review; vendor remediation plans with enforceable clauses; right to reduce or terminate for misrepresentation or non-remediation.
enforcement: Complaints go to the agency accessibility coordinator; WaTech policy governance; ADA Title II complaints to US DOJ.
notes: Washington is stricter than the federal floor (WCAG 2.2 AA). Sunset review is 2027-12-10.
